subject.title: refactor(plugin-sdk): isolate core session state from plugin mutations

question: Should `getAcpSessionManager()` intentionally stop returning the shipped concrete `AcpSessionManager` instance in the current release line so private session coordination can be isolated before recovery writers land?
rationale: The facade is the cleanest isolation boundary, but accepting an unversioned concrete-to-structural identity change for a shipped Plugin SDK API is a product and compatibility decision that tests cannot resolve.

options.title: Accept the sealed facade now
options.body: Approve the identity break, retain the current facade design, and require explicit upgrade documentation for plugins using class identity or constructor access.

options.title: Phase in a new getter
options.body: Add a separately named facade getter and defer removal of the concrete getter, which preserves compatibility but blocks full isolation until a defined breaking-version boundary.

options.title: Pause the recovery series
options.body: Keep the shipped getter unchanged and postpone private recovery-state producers until the repository is ready for a versioned SDK break.

recommendation.title: Accept the sealed facade now
recommendation.body: Approve the identity break, retain the current facade design, and require explicit upgrade documentation for plugins using class identity or constructor access.

likelyOwner.reason: The root CODEOWNERS assignment and scoped Plugin SDK policy make `steipete` the strongest available owner for this public-contract choice.
